$description: Wave 3 (W3 Forms-Core, D-015) component tokens for Input/Textarea/PinInput/InputGroup — every field in this wave shares this one file. Aliases semantic/* only (never primitive/* directly). bg uses `color.surface.inset` (the recessed step of the D-008 surface ladder) so text fields read as a sunken affordance vs. Button's raised fill — same physical-elevation logic braun-flat.md already applies system-wide, just applied to the 'receiving' side of an interactive control instead of the 'acting' side. border.default uses `color.border.interactive` (D-014 pattern, NOT `border.hairline` — hairline was designed for quiet dividers and fails the 3:1 UI-boundary minimum here too, same reasoning as Button outline's neutral border) — self-checked at 4.07:1 (light) / 3.91:1 (dark) against `surface.inset`, both pass (re-measured 2026-08-14 via `tooling/contrast-check.mjs` after D-028's neutral-ramp hex rebuild — the neutral ramp's hue correction moved these two numbers slightly off their original 3.47:1/4.20:1 self-check, both still clear the real 3:1 UI-boundary floor with margin, dark theme's margin just got closer to the floor, from +1.20 down to +0.91). border.invalid reuses `color.action.danger.default` (already the D-014-fixed AA-safe step, not a new color) — 5.74:1 / 7.90:1 against `surface.inset` (also re-measured 2026-08-14, moved from the original 6.05:1/6.87:1 for the same reason, still clears both floors). Hover state is NOT a new border color (no token here needs to carry it) — component CSS bumps `border-width` from hairline to thick instead, a non-color/non-shadow state cue per braun-flat rule 4 that can't regress contrast since the color is unchanged. disabled uses `border.hairline`/`text.disabled` — WCAG's contrast minimums are exempt for disabled controls (inactive, not read as content), so their sub-3:1 measurement on `surface.inset` is expected and not a finding.
